lines.text: A step is three files: a descriptor (data only), a compute module and a thin shell that exports `pipeline.step(descriptor, compute)`. File names are hyphenated and need not match the slug; §1 table 1b lists every step's real paths. `scripts/steps/_schema/step.schema.json` is the vocabulary; prose never adds a field. Behaviour lives in descriptor data, a declared check, a shape rule or (last resort) a new schema field, never only in code (Rule 1).
lines.why: One place says what a step is, and the schema, not a reviewer, decides what is valid.

lines.text: All 20 categories are present and every field is answered; write `"none"` (with a why where the schema asks) instead of leaving a field out. Declare at least one check.
lines.why: An omitted field cannot be told apart from a forgotten one; "none" is a decision someone made.

lines.text: Use the closed vocabulary: full-word archetypes; a lock id unique across manifest, one-time and backfill scripts; `guards.schema_drift` none/propagate/pause (rule id V3, alias SPEC122A-V3, which is not the V3 standard); staleness as scope × trigger; typed `empty_source`; and the cross-step majority forms (`batch`, `spec_version`, terminal ids, flat emits, notes keys). The old `outputs.writes[].replay` / `append_unsafe` field is deleted (V4, now history).
lines.why: Shared names let one library, one gate and one admin page read every step the same way.

lines.text: Take the archetype from the code: PH-0 derives it, and the census (`step-archetype-census.json`) must agree with the descriptor (#25). The archetype selects the required and forbidden categories. A step whose only write is a snapshot it exists to record is a RECORDER, not an ASSERT with a hidden write.
lines.why: The archetype drives which fields are required, so a wrong label silently drops checks.

lines.text: Where a machine can derive a descriptor value, it is gated rather than trusted: `mode_select` per archetype and emit types that match the captures (#47).
lines.why: A value the machine can check should never be the author's word alone.

lines.text: The verdict comes only from check rows. Each row is PASS, WARN (through `warn_limit` / `warn_limit_from_config`) or its declared severity. `checks_failed` counts FAIL rows and `checks_warned` counts WARN rows. A metric that is never zero is WARN with a stated retighten condition; INFO is only for a purely descriptive counter. A uniqueness invariant is a check row, not a throw. A legacy exclusive ceiling becomes an inclusive `ceiling_max` with a declared deviation.
lines.why: A parallel boolean or a severity chosen to dodge red hides failures from the run row and the admin page.

lines.text: A rule kept inside compute is still written down: as a check's `why`, or as an Intent Ledger row naming where it lives, never only as a code comment (`checkPreservedInComputeHasWhy`).
lines.why: Nothing about a step's behaviour may live only in code.

lines.text: EXTERNALIZED. Every number a step, gate, admin surface or tool uses is a registered logic variable or an exact zero. Step variables are named `<slug>_<name>`; a name shared by two or more steps comes only from the closed `SHARED_LOGIC_VARIABLES` map, and legacy shared names are renamed by migration with values carried. Unit constants and definitional windows are pinned (min = max). Runner and gate numbers are pinned `step_*` / `gate_*` / `tooling_*` variables. A missing `logic_variables` row fails the run; `on_invalid` is `fail` for any verdict- or write-affecting variable. A variable is retired by a `config.retired[]` declaration, never deleted. A model constant ratified elsewhere becomes a variable with its existing value as default.
lines.why: The operator tunes the system from the admin page; a literal in code is a setting nobody can see or change.

lines.text: Compute is pure. It receives `ctx` (config with `$meta`, clock, catalog, descriptor, `withinLimit`), reports every check value through `ctx.report(id, value)` and returns rows, a `write_plan` or `records_meta`. The runner owns every read set-up, write, transaction, session GUC (`execution.read_gucs`), catalog probe (`guards.requires` / `ctx.catalog`), calendar date (`ctx.clock` in `pipeline_timezone`) and the verdict. An ASSERT may read `ctx.pool` read-only over declared relations (R-CA (i)). Compute never branches on PostGIS; it never reads `logic_variables` SQL; a config value aliased inside a check body still counts as compute deciding (PURITY-G7). Gate E purity codes PURITY-G0…PURITY-G13 must read zero for a new conversion; the escape-hatch ban is an ast-grep rule.
lines.why: Pure compute can be tested with plain inputs, replayed from captures and reviewed without a database.

lines.text: Compute reads the `ctx` shape the runner's dispatch for its descriptor actually builds (a multi-primary INGESTOR gets `acquired.primaries[id]` and `written.by_target.<table>`, not the flat shape), and its compute lock builds that ctx through the real dispatch, stubbing only DB and network answers.
lines.why: A hand-built ctx in a test can pass while the real run reads zeros.

lines.text: Output is observable. `emits[]` equals what the captures emit and stays flat; dynamic-keyed telemetry rides a check row's `detail`, capped by a variable. A step that can skip declares a `when:"pre"` check; one that can scope-defer also declares a `deferred_to_full` terminal. Every run row carries the propagated `chain_run_id`.
lines.why: A skipped or deferred run must say why in its own audit table, and runs correlate by id, not by time window.

lines.text: Declare write discipline per write target, never per step: mechanic ⊥ guard ⊥ scope ⊥ retract. A banned write shape ships only with a dated, SHA-anchored `grandfathered.json` entry naming its why; guard `none` needs a why. A target on an RLS-enabled table declares `guards.requires: rls_bypass_or_policy`. One upsert binds at most 65,535 parameters, so the batch keeps the measured worst case under it.
lines.why: Write safety differs per table; a per-step answer is wrong for at least one target.

lines.text: A destructive retraction declares a truthful crash posture (`recovery.interrupted`) and a `recovery.before_image`; the library writes the before-image before retracting, and the runner forces FULL after an interrupted run.
lines.why: A run killed half-way must never leave a half-retracted table that the next run calls unchanged.

lines.text: Declared equals witnessed. Acquisition reads go in `inputs.reads`; measurement reads (check SQL, emits) in `checks[].reads`; per-mode statement counts in `outputs.write_inventory.by_mode`; version pins in `staleness.pins`; invalidators in `outputs.invalidates[]` with a closed `by`. Fast invariant #44 traces what the step really runs and fails any gap; an unresolved invalidator fails (#44 (i)); a pin on a producer still awaiting captures prints OWED. Prior-run baselines accept only completed/completed_with_warnings runs.
lines.why: The cross-step ledger is only true if it is measured, never re-typed.

lines.text: Every frozen enum value and every `execution.*` declaration has a disposition in its registry: executed (with a named executor or check), descriptive, or retired.
lines.why: A field that looks enforced but has no executor is a promise nobody keeps.

lines.text: The step is admin-verifiable: its registry, description, table-map and telemetry entries are derived from the descriptor (#51); range badges come from declared check bounds; each logic variable shows whether it is in effect (#53).
lines.why: The operator checks a step's output on the admin page, so the page must be derived, not hand-kept.

lines.text: A priced or modelled output declares the population it is for, as a query bound on the producing step.
lines.why: A number without its population cannot be checked or compared.

lines.text: Overrides are honest: `override.dry_run` is `"none"` unless the step honours it, and per-invocation row caps (`--limit=N`) are retired by deviation.
lines.why: A dry run that writes, or a cap that hides rows, makes the run report false.

lines.text: Phases run acquire → validate → write → score. Every "before X" guarantee in the owner spec becomes a `pre_write` check carrying an `order_guarantee` whose anchor is a literal sentence of that spec.
lines.why: A FAIL reported after rows are already written is a guarantee broken.

lines.text: A source-version skip is taken only when the target is non-empty.
lines.why: Skipping on an unchanged hash over an empty table leaves it empty for good.

lines.text: Primaries: a `ckan_datastore` primary is first-class (null geometry, targetless, union groups, per-member truth); a PDF document set is an acquisition format.
lines.why: Each source form gets one library path instead of a per-step reader.

lines.text: Derived secondary targets are written from a runner-owned prior-state read inside the primary transaction; one may be non-fatal (`on_error: warn_row`) with a declared zero-bound WARN check.
lines.why: The derived write stays atomic with its source and a failure still shows up as a row.

lines.text: A `written:"seen"` column is a runner-clock column touched for every fed key and excluded from the guard; its target declares `idempotent_rerun: "declared_drift"`, and the rerun proof passes only when rewritten == touched exactly.
lines.why: The touch rewrites rows on every run by design, so `zero_writes` would be a false claim.

lines.text: Worked examples (one step each): load_parcels replaces geometry only on a material change beyond a variable tolerance; close_stale_permits folds into load_permits' declared retraction; coa made its change-detection hash timezone-independent at the cost of one measured re-upsert.
lines.why: Shows how the general rules were applied where they were first needed.

lines.text: `mode_select` is `tri_state`, or `none` with a `full_rescan` invalidator (the mode gate itself is R-BH (i), on core.5). Crash posture is `force_full_on_next_run`, and an autonomous FULL run happens only on a chain whose `chain_args` declare `--full`.
lines.why: A destructive rescan must be chosen on purpose, never by accident after a crash.

lines.text: `runLinkPhase` (shape `link`) serves more than one LINK family through opt-in arms; counter names come from the match plan. Other LINK steps run their own phase: shape `link_keyed` (`runLinkKeyedPhase`), `link_column` (`runLinkColumnPhase`); a MATCHER runs `runCascadePhase` (shape `cascade`). §1 table 1a lists which step uses which. A match plan may also declare a closed `extra_counters` set, summed per batch (R-IG, from the bundled RE-FREEZE night).
lines.why: One library path, not a copy per link step.

lines.text: Worked examples: a link-rate floor's denominator is the entity population, not the source-row count (link_wsib); a full-rescan LINK may keep its junction current with a declared material-geometry trigger (`guards.requires`, link_parcel_abutments).
lines.why: Shows the rules applied where they were first needed.

lines.text: Open operator question Q-B1: a better neighbour front-setback estimator (`front_setback_est_m`; owed to the Spec 130 lane). Since 2026-10-19 (operator ruling; Spec 130:93, Spec 131 LC-58, Spec 69a M-205(1) dated note) averaging is evaluated: max(neighbour estimate + `fya_porch_allowance_m`, the zone default), always "needs survey"; Q-B1 stays open only for a better estimator. A reader must not read a parcel with no abutment pairs (deleted until the next run by R-CR's trigger) as "no neighbours". Separately, R-CR's trigger form is replaced by the fleet keyed-delete arm when that lands; that does not close Q-B1. (124a R-CR's own cell still says averaging stays `not_evaluated` until Q-B1; that cell is stale, owed to a ruling lane.)
lines.why: An unanswered question stays visible on its own line, next to the rule that raised it.

lines.text: Accuracy is a sampled precision/recall against a before-image, recorded at each repair, never a self-consistent predicate.
lines.why: A matcher graded against itself always passes.

lines.text: No Layer-1 skip: a legacy skip gate moves into the write scope as a declared deviation, or, if it has no runner home and no lineage column, is knowingly retired.
lines.why: An ENRICHER that skips whole runs hides rows that changed upstream.

lines.text: `runEnrichPhase` is generic: hooks are optional `enrich_hooks` declarations and intervals come from config. Pass DML goes through `ctx.exec(writesRef, sql, params)`; scope-ledger hygiene DELETEs are library-owned, and a guard-suppressed hygiene action emits one WARN row. Updated counters belong to whichever mechanism wrote the rows this run.
lines.why: Writes stay behind the runner seam, and counters are not double-counted.

lines.text: `execution.maintenance` may declare a dead-tuple-ratio dynamic-target arm, measured once and shared.
lines.why: Vacuum decisions follow the table's real state, from one measurement.

lines.text: `recovery.reset` is not none. `materialize_form` is `insert_select` or `rows` (rows computed in JS; the runner owns reads, writes and transactions); batch size comes from config.
lines.why: Rebuilds must be resumable, and JS rows must not bring their own I/O.

lines.text: Batch size comes from config. A one-time backfill leaves its chain once a measured run inserts 0 rows (backfill_realtor_permit_trades).
lines.why: A finished backfill should stop costing a chain slot.

lines.text: `outputs`, `recovery` and `counters` are none. Compute may read `ctx.pool` read-only over declared relations (R-CA (i), on core.9, corrects older text that says no pool is reachable); vocabulary-coverage reads use a runner-owned READ ONLY snapshot.
lines.why: An ASSERT measures; it must not change what it measures.

lines.text: Worked example: assert_schema checks at chain start that every declared logic variable has a DB row.
lines.why: A missing variable is caught before any step reads it.

lines.text: A RECORDER's `outputs` is an object (never `none`) and its snapshot write is declared in `outputs.writes[]`. Either `runRecorderPhase` executes it (shape `recorder`), or the step declares no shape and compute returns a `write_plan` that the runner executes after compute (`runWritePlan`, R-CD). (`outputs.publish` was deleted at a RE-FREEZE; Spec 124 §3's Rule 7 table still names it.)
lines.why: The snapshot is the step's purpose, so it is declared, not hidden.

lines.text: Four gates: a kill switch or injected transport, an exactly-once ledger, captured intended effects, and a dry run. Outside calls are replayed from recorded responses.
lines.why: An effect on the outside world cannot be rolled back, so it must be switchable, counted once and rehearsable.

lines.text: Reconcile runs as a step at the head of the sources chain. A slug whose concern the runner owns (`reconcile`, `observe_chain`) is a declared `runner_owned` exemption, not a conversion; a step is retired, not converted, only under a closed predicate.
lines.why: Every chained slug has exactly one honest status.

lines.text: Seam validation and chain-end synthesis derive from declared step edges; a chain step row's status is derived from its verdict (PASS → completed, WARN → completed_with_warnings, a covered FAIL → completed_with_errors); a hard-coded `'completed'` is retired.
lines.why: A chain that says completed after a FAIL is lying.

lines.text: A step's stage is declared data in `converted.json` `pending[]`: `red_suite` → `descriptor_only` → `compute_ported` → `runner_wired` → `shape_clean` (or `shape_clean_pending_recapture`) → converted. Red tests are declared there, never a code skip. The declared stage alone decides which gates cannot yet be answered (`stageAwaitsCaptures`); a pending row with no descriptor file does not block whole-registry selection.
lines.why: Progress is visible and a half-built step is graded for what it is.

lines.text: The commits are ① red suite + descriptor, ② compute + runner (the shell swap), ③ cutover into `converted[]`. A pending step lands ② at `compute_ported` with its legacy shell live, and may swap its shell before ③ only once every declared upstream (`inputs.reads.steps`) is converted, or pending past ② and not awaiting captures (`stageAwaitsCaptures`); fast invariant #54 checks this, and an unregistered or unknown upstream fails.
lines.why: A downstream step never runs on a converted shell before its producer.

lines.text: A net-new step (no legacy predecessor) has no PRE capture; its G8 reference is its committed POST. It is accepted as net-new only with the full R-DK evidence set: census `legacy: "none"`, no git history of the script before its descriptor, no `legacy_citation`, a `recapture.json` entry with `via` bracket or env, a red-evidence artifact (gate K) and a rerun-zero proof on every POST. Otherwise fast invariant #22 refuses it by name, and any PRE file on an accepted slug is RED.
lines.why: There is nothing older to compare against.

lines.text: A cutover stages every owner spec named in the system map, or declares `Spec-diff: N-A` (#43). Target Files are generated into the owner spec; every spec that names a chained step classifies it; fleet counts are derived from registries, never retyped.
lines.why: Specs and registries stay in step with the code without anyone remembering to update them.

lines.text: Captures are reproducible from committed data alone: every capture has a `recapture.json` entry, and `node scripts/analysis/capture-step-golden.js --replay-all` prints the retake commands from those entries (plain and env captures first, then brackets); capture pairs follow the declared chain variance. Every harness run is ledgered as captured, never a baseline. PRE captures are committed before re-runs. A post witness trace with no golden capture and no `recapture.json` entry is an orphan: it is deleted by literal path only when a recipe-backed trace of the same slug witnesses a superset of its statement fingerprints, otherwise it gets a recipe and is retaken (R-IJ).
lines.why: A capture nobody can retake proves nothing.

lines.text: A forced-write table is proven by a bracket: a perturbation cohort (when a guard includes the step's own stamp), delete-and-reinsert (INSERT-only), or derived-status (derived targets), counted through gate G's `count_path`. A PRE taken with a retired input argv stands in only under a closed predicate.
lines.why: A rerun that writes nothing proves nothing about a guarded write path.

lines.text: The golden differential is a mechanical fingerprint gate (G8, #38/#40). Every diff is explained only in `docs/reports/golden/<slug>/explained-diffs.json`, citing a Defect Ledger id; an unexplainable differential stops the work.
lines.why: A commit message saying "diff is fine" is not evidence.

lines.text: A step that calls a paid or outside API is captured and replayed from committed recorded responses.
lines.why: Tests and captures must not spend money or depend on someone else's uptime.

lines.text: A class-A behaviour (Spec 123 risk class A) is proven by a both-directions lock, shown red then green (scorecard G7; mutation testing is not a gate). Tests write before-images into a per-file sandbox, never the real golden tree. A live test proves its child process completed before asserting on its output.
lines.why: A test that cannot fail, or that reads output that never arrived, proves nothing.

lines.text: A same-statement write guard is not a chain-order edge. ORDER rows with neither endpoint converted and unproduced reads whose inserter is unconverted are counted against a shrink-only ceiling, not hard. Gate D reads one converted-set view.
lines.why: The ledger stays strict for converted steps without blocking on legacy ones.

lines.text: One command grades a step: `node scripts/analysis/step-validate.mjs --step=<slug>` (or `--all`, `--staged`, `--fast`). It validates the DATA (descriptor, fast invariants) and the scorecard grades the PROCESS; it runs in the hooks, never as a separate track.
lines.why: One integrated answer, the same at the desk and in the hook.

lines.text: The scorecard gates G0–G9 (Spec 123 §6; aliases SCORECARD-G0…SCORECARD-G9, not the Gate E purity codes): G0 boundary freeze, G1 archaeology, G2 churn × complexity, G3 Intent Ledger (only tables with a Disposition column are scored), G4 risk class, G5 seam map, G6 classification with Defect Ledger ids, G7 test adequacy, G8 differential, G9 §R Reflection. Ship bar: ≥14/17 with G6–G8 full; with E3 on it is 17/17. Markdown header and separator rows are never counted as data.
lines.why: The assessment is graded by machine, the same for every step.

lines.text: `standard=V3` prints only when all nine R-EY conditions hold, fail closed: (1) compute purity clean, (2) no gate-ledger allowance, (3) #44 PASS with nothing attributed, (4) no blocking registry failure, (5) no stage-gated red, (6) G0–G8 at max with no other hard stop, (7) the five words all PASS with nothing deferred, (8) no unmet `cutover_prereq`, (9) every exception naming the step cites a register id. Otherwise it prints `standard=V2 (fails: …)`. E1 (ratchet: a step that read V3 never drops) and E2 (cutover gate) are on; E3 (every converted step V3) is built off behind `gate_v3_hard_gate_enabled`. R-IH stage 1: `step-validate` prints an advisory `R-EY (9) why-only` line for each step with a deviation whose only register id is in `why`, plus a run total; no verdict changes until stage 3 reads `adjudicated_by` only.
lines.why: One list replaces the older "five words", "six parts" and "four conditions"; the label means the same thing everywhere.

lines.text: An operator decision found only in a plan or assessment (a pilot plan's rulings, an accepted deviation) is recorded as a register row before a step can cite it: the V3 condition-9 backfill recorded 33 such decisions as rows R-FI…R-GO (124a §B21/§B22), and each exception entry they govern cites its row. A citation on a converted descriptor's `deviations[]` entry is appended on the bundled RE-FREEZE night, because the edit moves the capture fingerprint. That night is split (R-II): night 1 carries the citations, and the refresh_snapshot producer-read waits for its own RE-FREEZE at permits ③.
lines.why: Condition (9) needs a resolvable id on every exception, and a decision that lives only in a plan file is invisible to the gate.

lines.text: An exception entry with no operator decision found (the condition-9 census class c) goes to the operator as a family ruling, recorded by decision log and register row like any other: the 2026-10-20 rulings are R-HN…R-HZ (V3 Exception Rulings page and chat CHAT-22) and the CoA cutover rulings R-IA…R-IF (R-IB and R-IC also cover enrich_permits' twin deviations, operator CHAT-24). A conversion retires a legacy audit row, `records_meta` key, constant row or log-only query only when the entry cites a consumer grep with zero readers or shows the counted mechanism is gone (R-HR, a named exception to Spec 123 §3.1); a legacy defect corrected inline is ratified per entry, never as a general rule (R-HQ). Citations on a fingerprint-locked descriptor ride the bundled RE-FREEZE night.
lines.why: Condition (9) needs every exception to cite a ruling, and a family ruling with its evidence condition stated once is cheaper to check than one ruling per entry.

lines.text: When no rung answers, use the protocol: one pass discovers and proposes (closed Intent Ledger vocabulary); a different party adjudicates, named and dated; the ruling gets a dated register row in Spec 124 §5 (or a 124a LIVE REGISTER section) that answers the seven admission questions and names a lock; the same commit adds the both-directions test and amends the spec; a pilot-local defect becomes a ruling only if it will recur in another archetype; a document move is tool-performed and verified by a line-set diff. Cited ids must resolve.
lines.why: A rule without a lock is not a rule, and the person who found a problem does not get to rule on it.

lines.text: Resolution ladder: ground the problem (query, grep, read; cite the owner spec from the system map); classify it CONTRACT / INCIDENTAL / DEFECT; resolve at the first fitting rung (descriptor, declared check, logic variable, library change, shape rule, new schema field); if none fits or two conflict, go to the protocol; add a both-directions test and re-run the golden capture; record a Defect Ledger id and a §R Reflection entry when it may recur. Route each learning to the most enforced artifact that can hold it.
lines.why: The cheapest enforced answer wins, and lessons are kept where a machine reads them.

lines.text: Where the standard is written: Spec 122 is the standard (the live schema and behaviour) and the Spec 124 register is the policy; on policy the register governs, on the schema and behaviour Spec 122 does. Spec 123 is the standard for the conversion procedure and its G0–G9 gates. This handbook is Spec 132, generated from both through the rule map; cite a line as `Spec 132 §<line id> (R-xx)`. Every spec opens with one role banner (authority register, standard, design, historical, generated handbook); a historical spec adds no rule id, so a new rule goes to the register.
lines.why: Each question has one home, and a reader knows from the first lines what a spec may decide.

lines.text: Operator decisions are transferred by generator, never by hand: each set of rulings (a review-page export or a chat ruling with its quote, and any later amendment with its quote) is committed verbatim as `docs/reports/decisions/<date>-<slug>.json`; `node scripts/analysis/decision-log.mjs --write` emits a register-row skeleton per approved decision, and every approved decision becomes a register row (Spec 124, Spec 69a or Spec 131 by subject) that cites `<log stem>#<decision id>`; `--check` at pre-commit fails on an uncovered decision or a citation of an unknown one.
